stage_configuration.evidence_type: Serialized PPtr resolution and structural parsing with original metadata/wrapper declaration consistency
stage_configuration.schema_boundary: AssetReferencer first custom PPtr; MStage leading stages vector fully consumes this object; MStageRecord first three declared fields only. Other MStageRecord fields are opaque. Serialized PPtr widths are 12 bytes; these offsets are not native field offsets.
stage_configuration.runtime_boundary: The scene-to-level convention and matching SceneName/StageController prefix are corroboration; this static configuration does not establish which save-state value is selected at runtime.

title_button_bindings.evidence_type: Complete structural parse of these serialized Button objects, with original metadata field names and interop enum constants
title_button_bindings.schema: MonoBehaviour prefix; Selectable Navigation(mode,bool+align,4 PPtrs), transition Int32, ColorBlock(22 floats), SpriteState(4 PPtrs), AnimationTriggers(5 strings), interactable bool+align, targetGraphic PPtr; Button.onClick PersistentCall vector; each call follows target/assembly/method/mode/ArgumentCache/callState declaration order. All supported objects consume exactly EOF.
title_button_bindings.limitation: Serialized persistent bindings establish configured targets/method names and listener modes; they do not prove a click occurred or the timing of runtime transitions.

animation_reference_and_event_boundary.schema_boundary: AssetReferencer.FadePanel is a PPtr after 27 leading reference fields, corroborated by original declaration order and generated property types. Animator class95 parses only owner/enabled/avatar/controller through byte40. AnimatorController class91 and AnimationClip class74 parse only NamedObject aligned name; remaining blobs are preserved opaque.
animation_reference_and_event_boundary.event_evidence_boundary: Function-name byte occurrences are bounded observations inside specific clip objects, not AnimationEvent parsing. No event count/time/function dispatch or controller-to-clip association is established. A reliable Unity 6000 AnimationClip/AnimatorController schema or runtime trace remains required to prove fade-completion event wiring.

limitations: No game execution or REA session was opened; this is static serialized-resource evidence.
BuildSettings has ten ordered scene paths; correspondence with levelN uses the standard player layout and observed component identities, not an extra explicit mapping table.

The BuildSettings tail and most custom component payloads are preserved but not fully schema-decoded; the supported MStage table, MStageRecord prefix and Button objects have explicit per-section decode boundaries.
Serialized enabled/active values and resolved parent chains do not establish actual runtime Awake/Start execution or later scene lifetime.
StageController raw prefix values, metadata field order, and wrapper enum declaration are distinct corroborating observations; scene filenames alone do not determine StageType.
This component-name selection is not a claim to enumerate all initialization behavior, dynamically created objects, scene unloads, or save-data-dependent branches.
